answer: Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. Fingerprints are counted in hollow, as a result the distribution is public, and cipher lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a willow header, so 3310 keys running one model collapse to a single share. That is 40 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
